messages:
acme-integrations: hey team — since the schema migration last night our ingest to the vecdb is spiking rejects. getting ~18k rejects in the last hour, errors say dimension mismatch. billing also jumped unexpectedly. any quick mitigations? :grimacing:

maya: thanks for the ping. can you paste one example error line and the model name you switched to? also does the client side send any dim header? :eyes:

acme-integrations: sample from indexer logs below — migration finished ~2026-03-16T22:10Z

```
ERROR indexer: doc=acme:items:10042 reason="vector dimension mismatch" expected=1536 actual=128
payload_summary={"model":"text-embed-2025-quant","input_count":1}
```

acme-integrations: client is calling our embed pipeline with the new model container that was rolled out by infra. we thought dims were compatible but looks like the new quantized model produces 128-d vectors for some inputs.

aj: indexer-bot also fired alerts — cc'ing logs: :warning:

indexer-bot: alert: indexer.rejections.rate > 100/min for cluster vec-prod-2; top reason=dim_mismatch; recent sample ids=[10042,10045,10096]

karla: quick thought — are we mixing two different embed model variants across streaming batches? if previous stored schema expects 1536 we need to either 1) route requests to a 1536 variant, 2) transpose/backfill converted vectors, or 3) stop accepting new 128-d vectors and queue them. which can you do quickly?

acme-integrations: we can pin the routing to the old variant for new requests. but we need to decide what to do about the 18k rejected rows in the buffer/backfill queue — they must be reprocessed, otherwise search is degraded and billing is strange.

maya: action plan proposal:
- short term: set routing override to text-embed-2024-base (1536) for acme workspace (reduces new rejects)
- triage: collect sample rejected doc ids and a small repro bundle (<=100 docs) that we can run locally
- backfill: run controlled backfill converting the 128-d outputs to 1536 by re-embedding with the pinned model, or mark them for reingest
- billing: file a billing investigation for the spike (possible double ingest attempts)

aj: commands to pin model via routes API (run as infra/admin):
```
# pin workspace to older embed model
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.ai/v1/routes/pin \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"workspace":"acme","route":"embeddings","model":"text-embed-2024-base"}'
```

karla: repro checklist for eng-indexer:
- upload a repro bundle (gzipped newline JSON) containing ~50 sample docs that the customer submits
- run the indexing job locally with the same indexer config and model mapping
- confirm error lines and capture shape header from worker logs (`X-Embed-Dims` or similar)

acme-integrations: uploading repro bundle now to the support share: s3://acme-support/repobundles/2123456789.gz :white_check_mark:

ryan: while backfill is planned, we should also patch indexer to fail faster (reject at client boundary) and emit a more actionable error: include expected_dim and supplied_dim in the API response body so customers can triage without looking into logs. filing small change request to eng-platform.

karla: for backfill options — two allowed approaches:
1) re-embed: run backfill that re-runs the embed model pinned to 1536 and upsert vectors (safe, costs compute)
2) convert/pad: not recommended for quality — only acceptable if there is a verified deterministic padding scheme and customer accepts accuracy loss

acme-integrations: we prefer re-embed. please share the backfill window and estimated cost. we need an ETA for completing the 18k docs.

maya: estimate (rough): 18k docs @ 0.006s/doc on dedicated pool => ~2.5 minutes of GPU time but with overhead maybe 30–45m queued; cost estimate ~ $42 in compute plus indexer ops. we'll confirm with infra.

aj: infra notes — to avoid interfering with production, we'll run backfill on a dedicated backfill queue (priority low). scheduled window tonight 03:00-04:00 UTC unless customer requests earlier.

acme-integrations: schedule is fine. can you also mark those rejected docs as "skipped" in billing until backfill completes? billing team needs to review.

maya: noted — opening billing ticket and temporarily marking the invoice items PENDING_ADJUST. billing will follow up.

karla: technical runbook snippet (indexer backfill):
```
redwood-cli backfill start \
  --workspace acme \
  --source s3://acme-support/repobundles/2123456789.gz \
  --model text-embed-2024-base \
  --shard-size 1000 \
  --concurrency 4
```

karla: will monitor logs and surface any rows that still reject. if we see heterogenous dims in stored DB (some old 1536 and some 128) we'll plan a small schema migration: add column vector_version + migration state, then migrate search index to use vector_version aware routing. but that is a longer change.

acme-integrations: thanks all — appreciate the quick plan. leaving us with these open items: 1) infra pin route, 2) run backfill tonight, 3) billing hold, 4) eng-platform error markup. please confirm when route pinned and when backfill job initiated. :pray:

maya: confirming next steps assigned:
- aj will pin route (ETA 10m)
- karla will kick the backfill job and monitor (ETA start 03:00 UTC)
- ryan files small api error improvement PR (tracking in ENG-7342)
- maya opens billing ticket and will follow up with customer

aj: route pinned to text-embed-2024-base for workspace=acme. changes propagated to routing layer :white_check_mark:

karla: backfill job queued (job id backfill-2123456789). I'll post logs here once it starts and update with progress every 10m.

indexer-bot: backfill-2123456789 status=queued priority=low submitted_by=karla

acme-integrations: great, standing by. thank you everyone.

maya: keeping this thread open until backfill completes and billing resolved. will close after final verification and a short postmortem note. :memo:
